title: Probing the Structure of a Novel Chalcogenide Multiferroic Crystal Cu1.14Mn0.77SiTe2.9
content: The coexistence of magnetic and ferroelectric ordering makes multiferroic materials unique to fundamental science [1-3]. These materials open a route to controlling magnetism by electric field and vice versa, along with a possible piezoelectric property [2, 3]. With promising applications in magnetic memory devices, transistors, sensors, and actuators, there has been significant efforts to explore and characterize multiferroic materials [2, 3]. While a large number of oxide multiferroics such as BiFeO3, TbMnO3, GaFeO3, NiTeO₆, Fe2Mo3O₈, DyFeWO₆ have been identified [3, 4], recent efforts have been focused on halides and chalcogenides due to their ability to maintain multiferroicity at thinner film thicknesses [4, 5-9].
